GLS plots at Chuan Grove and former Raffles Town Club site released, can yield 930 and 250 residential units
article:
Two residential sites under the Reserve List of the 2H2026 Government Land Sales (GLS) Programme have been released for sale.

The sites, located at Chuan Grove and Plymouth Avenue/Dunearn Road are available for application and can potentially yield about 930 and 250 residential units, respectively, said URA in an Oct 27 release.

A Reserve List site will be launched for public tender only when a developer has submitted an indicated minimum price that is acceptable to the government.

The Chuan Grove site is a 99-year leasehold residential plot with a site area of 341,170 sq ft and a maximum gross floor area (GFA) of 852,932 sq ft.

The Plymouth Avenue/Dunearn Road plot, which is the former Raffles Town Club site, is zoned residential with commercial on the first storey. The 99-year leasehold plot, measuring 122,573 sq ft, has a maximum GFA of 257,408 sq ft. This includes up to 26,910 sq ft of commercial space, which must include a supermarket of at least 10,764 sq ft.

Neither of the sites are likely to be triggered for sale, said Mark Yip, CEO of Huttons Asia. "Developers may choose to wait for the 1H2027 GLS Programme with the expectation that the sites could be shifted to the Confirmed List, he added.

"While both plots have their own merits, we do not expect them to be triggered for sale in the near term," commented Wong Siew Ying, head of research and content at PropNex.

Chuan Grove site

The Chuan Grove site is close to two other pots that were awarded last year to a joint venture between Sing Holdings and Sunway Developments (now Sunway MCL).

The developers plan to amalgamate the parcels, which will be the site of One Chuan Grove, a 99-year leasehold, 1,056-unit residential project planned for launch in February 2027, said Yip.

The project will add “ample supply” in the Chuan Grove area, leaving “little incentive for developers to trigger the site”, he added.

However, if tendered, he believes the site could fetch a top land rate of $1,300 to $1,400 psf per plot ratio (psf ppr). Sing Holdings and Sunway had paid land rates of $1,376 psf ppr and $1,331 psf for the two site s at One Chuan Grove.

Developers will likely monitor the take-up of the new project to gauge the area’s depth of demand, added PropNex's Wong.

Nearby, Kingsford Group’s 916-unit Chuan Park was launched in November 2024. The 99-year leasehold project occupies the former Chuan Park site that the developer purchased en bloc for $890 million.

The new Chuan Park is 99% taken up at an average price of $2,594 psf, based on lodged caveats as of Oct 27.

Plymouth Avenue/Dunearn Road site

The Plymouth Avenue/Dunearn Road site is a regular-shaped plot formerly occupied by Raffles Town Club. The club's lease for the land expired on Oct 17.

“It has attractive site attributes, being across from the Stevens MRT interchange station for the Downtown and Thomson-East Coast Lines,” said Wong.

It is also close to schools, including the Singapore Chinese Girls’ School and St. Joseph’s Institution; the National University of Singapore (Bukit Timah Campus), and Singapore Botanic Gardens.

Still, Wong believes incoming supply from other Core Central Region GLS sites that have been awarded, but not yet launched, will deter developers from triggering the site for sale.

The plots — comprising sites at Bukit Timah Road , Dunearn Road, Holland Plain, Peck Hay Road and River Valley Green — could potentially add over 1,700 new homes in the CCR, she noted.

title: Mushrooms, timber, upcycling and old buildings: PLP Architecture's quest for greener, more liveable spaces
article:
Mushrooms might seem an unlikely candidate for the next generation of sustainable building materials, but researchers are exploring how fungi could help reduce the carbon footprint of construction.

Mycelium, the root-like network of fungi, currently has potential applications in insulation, acoustic panels and internal partitions in buildings.

Among those experimenting with it is PLP Labs, the research and strategy arm of UK-headquartered PLP Architecture, which has been developing lightweight mycelium building blocks.

Reinforced with timber dowels and grown in biodegradable formworks, the blocks are still in the R&D stage, although prototypes have been showcased at exhibitions and events.

"More people are becoming aware of the potential of using biomaterials, including materials that can be grown, to reduce embodied carbon," says Tina Qiu, partner at PLP Architecture.

"They are also trying to source locally, which can lower emissions from transportation. Such materials may be more adaptable and better suited for the local environment."

Mycelium is just one avenue of research at London-based PLP Labs, whose work also spans other sustainable materials, circularity, and how the built environment can affect people’s health and well-being.

These interests also inform the firm's architectural projects around the world — from minimising the carbon footprint of construction to adapting existing buildings for new uses.

In Singapore, PLP's portfolio includes the completed Park Nova ultra-luxury condo on Tomlinson Road, as well as the upcoming The Clifford development in Raffles Place and the redevelopment of the Marina Square complex on Raffles Boulevard.

Speaking to EdgeProp Singapore , Qiu discusses which ideas and innovations are already finding their way into buildings, which are still being studied, and what could help bring more of them into wider use.

Growing the next generation of building materials

PLP Labs' experiments with mycelium biocomposites, conducted over three years, began on a small scale.

In a meeting room converted into a makeshift lab at the firm's London headquarters, an interdisciplinary team grew hundreds of fungal samples.

The initial experiments involved growing and casting mycelium into cubes and other simple geometric shapes, before the team tested how it bonded with organic materials such as wood and muslin cloth.

"We experimented with a lot of different fungi and found one that was able to cling onto timber dowels, which gave the blocks their structural integrity," Qiu says. The timber dowels provide internal reinforcement, helping create blocks that are sturdy yet lightweight.

The research took an encouraging turn when it became apparent that mycelium could be grown within biodegradable 3D-printed wood formworks into countless, complex shapes.

"The formwork can be printed from 3D printers using timber substrate, and a bio-based resin glue is able to hold it together," Qiu notes.

With this new technique in hand, the team put different mycelium samples through compression and bending tests at an engineering lab at the University of Cambridge to assess their strength.

By Clerkenwell Design Week in London in 2023, the research had yielded an installation, named Symbiocene Living, comprising 84 mycelium blocks grown over three months. The modular pieces could be arranged in infinite configurations, including as partitions, seating, planters and tables.

PLP subsequently showcased its innovative 3D-printed wood and mycelium technique at other major design festivals and events, including the RHS Chelsea Flower Show in 2025.

Held in London, the flower show featured mycelium columns developed by PLP in collaboration with landscape design firm Modular. The columns were grown entirely using recycled material salvaged from previous shows.

How far can mycelium go?

Besides being biodegradable and carbon-efficient, mycelium also has fire-resistant, insulating and sound-absorbing properties, as well as a high strength-to-weight ratio.

This versatility offers potential applications, including as insulation, acoustic panels, lighting fixtures and internal partitions — mainly in non-load-bearing capacities.

Other architects and designers around the world have likewise been exploring mycelium as a potential building material through temporary structures and installations, such as bio-bricks grown from corn stalks and mushrooms, and mycelium panels on timber frames.

Although its applications in the built environment are still limited, Qiu sees the gradual adoption already as a significant step forward.

Further R&D is needed to expand the use of mycelium in architecture and construction, particularly for external facades and structural components, to help steer the industry away from fossil fuel-based materials.

Although PLP has tested mycelium extensively in the UK, the firm has yet to trial its blocks elsewhere to understand how they behave in other environments.

“There has been interest to bring it to this part of the world [in Asia], but we haven’t had a purpose to bring it here yet,” Qiu says.

Engineered wood in buildings, from Rome to South Korea

Fungi may hold promise for the future of construction, but another natural material — timber — is already being used in buildings across the globe .

In particular, mass-engineered timber (MET) has become a more established alternative to conventional concrete and steel.

Its use can reduce embodied carbon, shorten construction times and add visual richness through timber’s natural grain, colours and textures.

MET comprises engineered wood products with improved structural integrity. It includes cross-laminated timber (CLT), which is made by bonding layers of timber at right angles.

Two examples of PLP’s work with engineered timber are developments currently in the pipeline: the new headquarters for Italy's Ministry of Environment and Energy Security in Rome, and the upcoming National Meteorological Center in Daejeon, South Korea.

In Rome, the 30,000 sq m (322,917 sq ft) building will have two CLT volumes with exposed timber interiors, a rooftop timber canopy embedded with solar panels, a biophilic ground floor and a full-height landscaped atrium.

The South Korean project combines CLT with recycled low-carbon steel in a hybrid structure to reduce embodied carbon, alongside passive shading and earth ducts. It is set to become the country’s first net-zero government building.

Understanding timber's natural ageing

In Singapore, the tropical climate affects how and where timber can be used in buildings, especially if it is exposed to the elements. This also means that greater care is often needed to maintain it.

Heavy rain, intense sunlight and humidity can change timber’s appearance over time. Termites may also be a concern if the wood is not properly maintained.

Still, Qiu emphasises that timber can withstand outdoor conditions without necessarily compromising its performance.

"The durability, robustness and structural integrity are completely there [and unaffected]. It's more of an aesthetic thing," she says.

For example, birch wood’s pale, creamy hues may gradually deepen to richer amber or golden-brown tones after prolonged exposure to sunlight and air. Harsh rain can also leave timber looking greyish.

Some people mistake these changes for signs of deterioration or structural damage, "but it’s absolutely not", Qiu notes.

Others may feel uncomfortable with the visual effects of weathering. "But it's a natural material… Pianos, violins — they all age naturally," she adds.

"I think, over time, people will become more aware that biomaterials have to be allowed to behave and age in their own way."

The Clifford: Integrating timber into its design

With Singapore’s weather conditions in mind, she reckons indoor and sheltered spaces are better suited to timber’s use in the city-state for now.

At The Clifford, an upcoming office and retail development in Raffles Place by Singapore Land Group (SingLand), PLP is introducing MET within glass-enclosed spaces or "floating boxes" at the tower's sky terraces. Timber is also planned for parts of the ceilings.

Meanwhile, the ground-level podium will feature mineral materials such as glass-reinforced concrete, which is significantly less carbon-intensive than standard concrete.

"The floating boxes will be constructed out of timber, which will not be directly exposed to the outside environment but are still very connected to the outdoor spaces and gardens at the sky terraces,” Qiu says. "That combination of timber and greenery is part of the focus on well-being."

A redevelopment of the former Clifford Centre , the 35-storey The Clifford brings together workplaces, health and well-being, sustainability and public life in the heart of the CBD, according to PLP.

"Incrementally, we’re seeing a shift. In Park Nova, there was no timber. In The Clifford, there’s a small amount of timber," Qiu says.

"We hope that in the next project we can bring in more timber into these environments."

Finding new value in old materials

Even as PLP explores alternative building materials, it is also finding ways to give existing structures and materials a new lease of life — including at its own office.

Last year, the firm relocated its headquarters to a larger, 22,850 sq ft space at The White Chapel Building in east London. PLP Labs spearheaded the research and strategy for the new studio’s design.

The team applied a circular fit-out approach, taking every opportunity to reuse, upcycle, repurpose and extend the life of materials.

Over the years, PLP had accumulated plenty of architectural samples — including glass, terracotta and metal components — from their projects.

"Every time we worked on a building, we would have hundreds of samples of glass to make sure it goes on the facade correctly," Qiu says.

"We also had a lot of terracotta tiles, as well as window and door assembly parts like knobs."

Instead of throwing the samples away, PLP worked with suppliers to crush them into aggregates. These were then embedded into terrazzo-style surfaces, such as worktops, in the new office. Repurposed marble was also transformed into new tables.

"So we can see these materials around us as we’re working. They give us a connection to the buildings we’ve designed, which is very unique and special to us," she adds.

PLP estimates that 92% of the materials from the previous headquarters were either reused or donated, while a further 7% was recycled. Only 1% was discarded.

The project diverted waste from the landfill, which saved 175.78 tonnes of carbon dioxide, according to the firm.

It also says it achieved a 75.4% reduction in embodied carbon as compared to conventional approaches to office design and renovation. The project turned out 68% cheaper than the cost of a typical London fit-out, too.

Where new furniture was needed, circular design principles likewise guided PLP's selection of materials.

"The new cabinets and shelves are made out of timber," Qiu says. "They are also movable, not fixed, so that we can be more flexible with the space later on without having to dismantle and reassemble them."

Marina Square: 'Good bones' stand the test of time

In Singapore, PLP is looking to apply similar principles to Marina Square’s redevelopment.

SingLand is partially redeveloping and repositioning the 9.2ha mixed-use complex into a 24/7 destination with residential, hospitality, office, retail, sports, wellness and culture components, designed by PLP and Singapore’s DP Architects.

Slated for completion by 2031, the project will include three new towers — a luxury condo, a mixed-use block with a new hotel and offices, and a serviced apartment block — alongside the existing trio of hotels.

At the same time, the four-storey shopping mall will undergo an asset enhancement initiative.

Qiu points to the value of a well-designed, future-proofed structure that allows a building to be adapted for new uses decades later.

She highlights this forward thinking in Marina Square, originally designed in the 1980s by the late American architect John Portman, who pioneered soaring multi-storey interior atriums and massive self-contained complexes.

"Some buildings, particularly those from the 1980s, had more future-proofing and were ahead of their time in terms of being well thought out and having good structures. They could be used for the long term," Qiu shares.

On that note, she says Marina Square’s retail podium has "good bones for additional interventions", with generous floor-to-ceiling heights that allow for different kinds of innovative spaces to be created within it.

The existing structure of the mall will thus be retained and adaptively reused with minimal demolition. New construction will be limited only to small zones that are necessary for future-proofing.

"That means we can reduce a huge amount of carbon because we don't have to demolish the building and dispose of it later,” Qiu adds.

Making every resource count

The team is also studying how they can recycle and upcycle materials stripped out of Marina Square’s mall — such as glass, partitions and furniture — as much as possible, while applying lessons from their London office redesign.

Among the possibilities being explored is adding recycled glass aggregates and terracotta fragments as accents in mineral-based materials.

Each of the three new towers may then have a slightly different accent in their facades and panels.

"But the base materials will still be mineral ones, which helps reduce embodied carbon. And we're trying to stay away from using metals," Qiu says.

"So the same principles in materiality are holistically applied to the Marina Square precinct masterplan."

While making better use of existing structures and resources is key, they must go hand in hand with efforts to lower operational emissions.

This could include designing efficient building systems and selecting materials that help enhance energy performance, such as facade glazing that minimises solar heat gain to reduce the need for air-conditioning.

"We have to consider both [materials and operations] in parallel," Qiu notes.

Patience to experiment and innovate

Across its research and projects, PLP continues to push the boundaries of what architecture can achieve, pursuing innovations to create more sustainable, healthier, vibrant and comfortable spaces.

Progress may come in small steps, but Qiu believes it is important to take the time to get things right — especially when working with alternative or experimental materials.

For instance, PLP Labs’ work on mycelium building materials has already made “quite a huge progression”, she says.

"From the outside looking in, things may seem to be moving quite slowly. But every step is very purposeful."

title: Seven Hillview Terrace factories up for tender at $51.6 mil; four more on sale for $33.6 mil
article:
A portfolio of seven terraced factory properties in Hillview Terrace within Bukit Batok have been launched for sale by public tender.

The adjoining 999-year leasehold properties — located at 36A, 36B, 38, 38A, 38B, 38C and 38D Hillview Terrace — have a guide price of $51.6 million, said Colliers in an Oct 27 release.

The plots span a combined site area of 31,199 sq ft, which means the price works out to about $1,655 psf on the land area.

While the plots are zoned for residential use under the URA Master Plan, they have been approved for general industrial use. They have a gross plot ratio of 1.62.

Buyers may acquire the site for continued industrial or warehousing use. As privately held factories, they are not subject to JTC approval.

Alternatively, the site’s underlying residential zoning allows developers the option to explore redevelopment.

Subject to approval, an additional 0.30 plot ratio may be granted for the site for residential redevelopment. This would raise the maximum allowable plot ratio to 1.92, Colliers added.

“The flexibility to retain the existing industrial use or explore future redevelopment should appeal to a broad range of owner-occupiers, investors and developers,” said Steven Tan, executive director for capital markets and investment services at Colliers.

The tender for the portfolio will close at 3pm on Dec 1.

Separately, Colliers is also marketing another group of properties in the area. Comprising four freehold semi-detached factories at 31, 33, 35 and 35 Annex Hillview Terrace, the portfolio is up for sale by private treaty with a $33.63 million asking price.

The four properties occupy 19,781 sq ft of residential land with a gross plot ratio of 1.62. Similar to the properties up for sale by tender, the site could potentially qualify for an additional 0.30 if redeveloped for residential use.

Together, the two portfolios represent around 50,980 sq ft of land.

The availability of the freehold portfolio gives buyers “another option to consider alongside the tender site”, said Tan. “For developers, the combination of contiguous land, residential zoning, and long leasehold and freehold tenures creates an opportunity that is difficult to replicate in the area.”

The latest industrial transaction in Hillview Terrace was the sale of a 999-year factory with a land area of 5,672 sq ft that fetched $8.5 million, or $1,499 psf.

Before that, two 999-year factories changed hands in April: One occupied a 6,836 sq ft site that fetched $9.3 million ($1,360 psf), and another, a 4,150 sq ft site that was sold for $5.8 million ($1,398 psf).

Why didn’t CLAR’s income growth reach unitholders?
CapitaLand Ascendas REIT
(SGX: A17U), or CLAR, owns 234 properties across Singapore, Australia, the US, the UK/Europe and Japan.
CLAR reports half-yearly.
For the first half of 2026 (1H2026), its distributable income grew 8.6% year on year (YoY) to S$359.4 million.
DPU rose just 0.1% to S$0.07482.
So where did the extra income go?
CLAR raised equity in both 1H2025 and 1H20-26.
The pie grew, but so did the number of slices.
Gross revenue rose 6.7% YoY to S$805.5 million, while net property income (NPI) climbed 6.2% to S$556.1 million, as acquisitions more than offset 2025 divestments.
Rental reversion was 8.5%, and management expects high single-digit reversions for the full year.
Occupancy dipped to 89.1% from 91.8% a year ago, or 90.3% excluding two newly completed properties.
Watch how CLAR funds its pipeline.
Its 39.7% aggregate leverage is the highest of the three, and its cost of debt is 3.5%.
It has another S$638.1 million of acquisitions announced and five ongoing projects worth S$507.2 million.
The proposed S$200.4 million sale of Kim Chuan Telecommunications Complex, at a 32% premium to valuation, will help.
If CLAR turns to unitholders again, though, DPU could stay flat even as income grows.

Mapletree Pan Asia Commercial Trust
(SGX: N2IU), or MPACT, owns 15 commercial properties across Singapore, Hong Kong, China, Japan and South Korea, with Singapore making up 61% of portfolio value.
For the first quarter of the financial year ending 31 March 2027 (1QFY2027), MPACT’s NPI fell 6.8% YoYto S$154.8 million.
DPU fell a milder 2.5% to S$0.0196.
Lower interest costs made the difference: MPACT used divestment proceeds to pay down debt, and finance expenses fell 18.4% YoY.
Its cost of debt improved to 2.94%, with aggregate leverage at 37.7%.
VivoCity carries the portfolio.
Its NPI grew 8.9% YoY after its Basement 2
asset enhancement
.
Rental reversion hit 13.5%, and tenant sales rose 4.9%.
Portfolio committed occupancy slid to 84.4% from 89.3% a year ago, with Japan at 56.0% and China at 82.4%.
Reversions were 29.2% in China and 9.1% at Festival Walk.
But repaid debt can only cut interest once.
For DPU to grow again, MPACT needs to fill space in Japan and China.
Festival Walk’s 18,800-square-foot reconfiguration offers some hope.
It began operating in July 2026 and delivers close to a 50% return on investment.

Can Singapore hold up MIT while it trims North America?
Mapletree Industrial Trust
(SGX: ME8U), or MIT, owns 135 properties across Singapore, North America and Japan.
It offers the highest yield of the three, and its DPU has fallen the most.
For 1Q20FY27, MIT’s NPI fell 8.5% YoY to S$122.3 million, and DPU dropped 4.9% to S$0.0311.
MIT lost income from three Singapore properties sold in August 2025, and from North American non-renewals and higher operating costs.
A weaker US dollar and costlier replacement
interest rate
swaps added to the pressure.
On the flip side, a 24.6% fall in borrowing costs and a bigger contribution from Japan softened the blow.
Still, DPU rose 0.6% quarter on quarter, mainly because there was no cyclical maintenance this quarter.
One quarter isn’t a trend, though.
Singapore is pulling its weight, with occupancy up to 94.3% from 93.4% three months earlier and rental reversion at 5.3%.
Japan stayed fully occupied.
North American occupancy slipped to 82.5% from 86.1%, though reversion there stayed positive at 2.2%.
MIT plans to sell S$500 million to S$600 million of North American assets, and each sale removes income.
It sold the Philadelphia Data Centre for US$14.5 million, above its US$13.9 million valuation.
It also signed about 364,500 square feet of North American leases, including a 10-year lease at Hawthorne Data Centre.
Aggregate leverage stood at 37.5%.

At MPACT and MIT, lower interest costs did much of that job, and that cushion has a limit.
At CLAR, the gap ran the other way: income grew, but new units soaked it up.

Compare the change in DPU with the change in NPI and distributable income, then trace the difference.

title: Nvidia vs AMD: Which Chip Stock Is the Better Buy Today?
article:
Nvidia
(NASDAQ: NVDA) and
AMD
(NASDAQ: AMD) are two of the leading players in the market for advanced AI chips.
Yet, their business models, profitability and valuations differ.
Nvidia is the more established – and far larger – company.
As of 16 October 2026, it had a market capitalisation of US$5.2 trillion, compared to AMD’s US$863 billion.
But there are benefits to being a challenger, and both companies have been swept up in the enthusiasm for
all things AI
.
Nvidia: The Dominant Player
Nvidia is the undisputed market leader in graphics processing units (GPUs), each of which can have many cores that allow for processing of complex operations simultaneously, making them suitable for training the large language models (LLMs) that are the foundation of generative AI.
Notably, Nvidia also owns the CUDA computing platform, which allows developers to use GPUs for general-purpose processing, and not just the graphics rendering they were traditionally designed for.
Many developers in AI have been trained to use CUDA, which only works with Nvidia chips, creating a barrier to entry for other chip companies.
Nvidia is the biggest beneficiary of the
AI boom
– its revenue rose by 3.5x to US$216 billion in its financial year ending January 2026 (FY2026), compared to FY2024.
Its margins are equally impressive, with a gross margin of 71% in FY2026. The company also generated nearly US$103 billion in cash from operating activities in the same year.
Part of this windfall has gone into investments and partnerships with key players in the AI ecosystem, from frontier labs OpenAI and Anthropic, to AI data centre operators such as
CoreWeave
(NASDAQ: CRWV).
Some market participants have likened these arrangements to circular financing, since all are important Nvidia customers.
Related articles:
Amazon and 2 Other Winners: 3 Growth Stocks to Buy Now and Hold for the Long Term
More Than Just Chips: Why the AI Revolution Needs These 5 Companies
AMD: The Upstart
AMD’s traditional strength was in making central processing unit (CPU) chips, which were initially overlooked when the AI boom first started.
However, the increasing focus on inference and AI agents means that demand for CPUs is expected to increase by 10x from 2025 to 2030.
Indeed, Muse. from
Meta Platforms
’ (NASDAQ: META), and OpenAI’s Dots, the two companies’ respective AI agents, both run on AMD’s EPYC-branded CPUs.
AMD is also challenging Nvidia in the GPU space with its Instinct product, which it is combining with its CPUs, networking, and ROCm software stack to create Helios, its fully integrated AI infrastructure offering.
Unlike CUDA, AMD’s ROCm is open-source and can run on GPUs from other manufacturers, even Nvidia’s.
If ROCm is able to attract more developers and users, it may even be able to breach the CUDA moat.
Hyperscalers from Meta to
Microsoft
(NASDAQ: MSFT) are spending huge sums of money on AI chips and looking for alternatives to Nvidia so it doesn’t exercise excessive market power.
This presents AMD with an opportunity to take market share from the leader.
Related articles:
3 US Stocks That Doubled in a Year: Should You Buy, Hold or Take Profits?
5 AI-Related Growth Stocks to Supercharge Your Investment Portfolio
Which Chipmaker Has the Stronger Business?
For now, Nvidia is still far ahead of AMD, which had US$35 billion in revenue for its financial year ending December 2025 (FY2025), 1.5x its FY2023 revenue.
But this was still just 16% of Nvidia’s top line for the comparable period.
Both have data centre businesses that are growing strongly.
In Nvidia’s most recent quarter, 2QFY2027, its data centre revenue grew by 2.2x to US$89 billion on strong demand for its cutting-edge Blackwell chips.
AMD’s data centre business experienced similar levels of year-on-year growth, with the segment’s revenue of US$6.7 billion being 2.1x the year-ago figure.
Yet, Nvidia’s business is far more profitable, a reflection of its market leadership.
For example, its 1HFY2027 net income margin was 66%, compared with AMD’s 17% for 1HFY2026.
Despite its market leadership, Nvidia isn’t resting on its laurels.
Earlier this year, it announced the Vera CPU, purpose-built for agentic AI, which it claims is twice as efficient as, and 50% faster than traditional CPUs.
Still, the desire from hyperscalers to see a viable alternative supplier to Nvidia should ensure that AMD gets its share of AI-driven demand.
AMD also stands to benefit from operating leverage, as fixed costs are spread across a larger business.
Its gross profit margin rose from 40% in 2QFY2025 to 54% in 2QFY2026, and is expected to reach 56% in 3QFY2026.
Looking ahead, both businesses must continue to innovate to stay ahead of the competition.
Size also gives Nvidia the advantage here.
In 1HFY2027, it spent US$13.4 billion on R&D, nearly 3x the US$4.9 billion AMD spent in its equivalent period.
It’s also worth noting that Nvidia’s R&D expenditure was just 7.5% of revenue over that period, compared to 22.6% for AMD.
Valuation and Risk
Given Nvidia’s superior economics, one might expect it to attract a premium valuation to AMD.
However, this is not the case.
Nvidia’s forward price-to-earnings ( P/E) ratio is 24.9x, while its PEG ratio (which accounts for expected earnings growth) is 0.5x.
The equivalent figures for AMD are 39.5x and 0.6x respectively.
Part of the explanation for this paradox is that AMD has already seen a significant run-up in its share price – it is 137% higher in the year to 16 October 2026.
Nvidia’s share price, in contrast, rose by just 13% over the same period.
Although both companies face similar risks, including the bursting of the AI bubble and the cyclicality of the
semiconductor industry
reasserting itself, AMD’s higher valuation also means that it is more susceptible to changes in investor sentiment.
Nvidia, meanwhile, might be doubly exposed to the underperformance of the companies in the AI ecosystem it has invested in.
In the past week, for example, CoreWeave’s share price has fallen by 24% as investors fret over its debt levels and ability to scale its business.
Get Smart: Which AI Chip Stock Would I Buy?
Nvidia and AMD offer two distinct ways to invest in the growth of AI computing.
Nvidia benefits from its established leadership, strong software ecosystem and proven profitability.
AMD offers the potential for significant growth and operating leverage if it successfully expands its market share.
However, given its superior economics and lower valuation, Nvidia might be the pick between the two, despite understandable scepticism about how much more a US$5.2 trillion company can grow.

article:
Deciding where to put your S$10,000, especially if it’s your first investment, can be terrifying.
Many investors choose between investing in individual stocks, which have greater potential to outperform the market, and
exchange-traded funds (ETFs)
, which offer instant diversification.
Both approaches have their advantages, so let’s look at which suits your needs better.
Option #1: Invest S$10,000 in an ETF
ETFs are baskets of stocks that track specific market indices or themes.
For example,
Vanguard Total World Stock ETF
(NYSE: VT) is a globally diversified ETF that holds almost 10,000 stocks.
For a more local approach,
SPDR Straits Times Index ETF
(SGX: ES3) tracks the
Straits Times Index
(SGX: ^STI) and contains 30 holdings.
ETFs lower the research burden because they simply hold whatever stocks are in the index they track and need little upkeep from you.
Investors should, however, watch out for fees and expense ratios, along with exchange rate fluctuation risks if they are investing in overseas ETFs.
Additionally, watch out for concentration risk.
The three local banks make up about 58% of the STI, so ES3 is heavily tied to the banking sector.

title: Spain eases data centre energy rules in win for Big Tech
article:
(Oct 27): Spain is easing rules for data center power usage and granting them more time to adapt to the new framework, after an initial government proposal faced strong industry backlash.

The revised draft introduces a transition regime over several years if data centre operators cannot match 80% of their energy consumption with renewable every hour of the day. Instead, under the new terms, projects will have to meet 60% of their electricity demand with renewable energy during peak hours, known as P1, until 2029, according to a copy of the draft seen by Bloomberg.

That requirement will climb to 70% in 2029, and then to 80% in 2032. The original tougher proposal would have introduced an 80% level all day immediately.

Spain has become one of Europe’s biggest markets for data centres, largely due to its cheap energy, with the likes of Amazon.com Inc, Microsoft Corp, Blackstone Inc and Merlin Properties Socimi SA all investing in the country. Industry group SpainDC expects IT capacity to rise nearly sixfold to 2.5GW from 2025 to 2030.

The trend faces opposition from the government, which says data centres could push electricity prices up for other consumers and add little value to the broader economy. Earlier this month, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said that they are an “extractive” business and officials have repeatedly criticised the facilities as financial deals rather than industrial projects.

The government first unveiled the plans in late August, heightening the tensions with industry.

See also: Sembcorp explores supplying low-carbon power to Singtel’s Nxera

Under the revised rules, data centres will also be required to increase the amount of renewable energy to 60% during the second-highest-demand periods, known as P2. This requirement will start in 2029.

The amended draft also relaxes a requirement that renewable power come from newly built power sites. They will be allowed to be 36 months old, compared with the previous proposal of 16 months. Solar plants will be removed from this requirement.

The government says the new rules will prioritise projects that are most likely to be built while discouraging companies from hoarding scarce grid capacity.

See also: Data centres get a reality check

The new proposal was sent to a key government consulting body Monday.

title: Vivian Balakrishnan visits Indonesia after natural gas cuts
article:
(Oct 27): Singapore Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan is scheduled to meet his Indonesian counterpart in Jakarta on Tuesday, days after Indonesia trimmed natural gas exports to the city-state.

A meeting with Indonesia’s Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir is scheduled for 3pm Jakarta Time, according to the country’s foreign ministry, which added that a joint statement is expected after the meeting.

Singapore’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment on the meeting.

Relations between the two countries have recently been rattled by Jakarta’s unexpected decision to trim natural gas supplies to the city-state.

Indonesian Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Bahlil Lahadalia said Monday that the cuts weren’t deep enough to constitute a breach of commercial contracts. Singapore’s Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry has said it’s checking with buyers to confirm that, but said Tuesday that it welcomes the “clarification” from Indonesia that its suppliers will honour their contracts.

That move had followed simmering tensions over the regional impact of haze from fires across Indonesia. President Prabowo Subianto and some members of its government directed angst toward unnamed neighbouring countries. Singapore is looking into 10 locally registered firms with Indonesia land operations.

See also: Singapore must work faster to vie with wealth hubs, says deputy PM

Separately, former Indonesian trade minister Muhammad Lutfi accused Singapore’s Temasek Holdings Pte Ltd and GIC Pte Ltd of pressuring MSCI Inc to consider downgrading the country’s stocks. Both state-owned funds denied the accusations.

title: Porsche profit holds firm as 911 cushions sales slump
article:
(Oct 27): Porsche AG’s profitability held up despite another sharp decline in vehicle sales, as demand for 911 sports cars and high-priced derivatives helped cushion the slump in China and weaker factory utilisation.

The automotive division posted a 6.9% operating margin for the first nine months, compared with 0.2% a year ago, while group operating profit recovered to €1.74 billion from €0.04 billion a year earlier. Revenue was €25.3 billion, versus €26.9 billion a year earlier.

Porsche retained its full-year forecasts for revenue of €35 billion to €36 billion and a group operating margin of 5.5% to 7.5%. Maintaining the outlook signals confidence in the fourth quarter, with analysts’ revenue estimates currently sitting just above the bottom of the range.

CEO Michael Leiters is working to repair a profit formula built on strong Chinese demand, high factory utilisation and a steady flow of lucrative new models. All three have weakened at once while US tariffs and Porsche’s costly reversals on electric vehicles have left the company, majority owned by Volkswagen AG, spending heavily just as its former growth engine contracts.

The 911 remains Porsche’s strongest defence. Deliveries of the sports car rose even as the wider business shrank, and buyers continued to favour expensive GTS, Turbo and GT versions. That mix is helping offset China and gaps left by the combustion-engine Macan and 718, but it cannot fully compensate for plants and development operations designed for much higher volumes.

Leiters’s first task is to shrink Porsche for a tougher era. The company plans to eliminate more than 9,000 positions, cut management ranks by 40% and lower the annual volume needed to break even to about 200,000 vehicles. He is also reducing development spending and concentrating resources on fewer, more profitable projects.

See also: Audi splits logos for China as carmaker fights to revive sales

Only then does Porsche intend to push decisively further upmarket. The strategy includes increasing prices of its most exclusive sports cars by about 20%, expanding bespoke and track-focused offerings and introducing models above the 911. The quarter offers early evidence of whether Porsche can preserve enough profit and cash during the cost-cutting phase to finance that more ambitious second act.

title: Orange boosts profit outlook after Africa, Middle East growth
article:
(Oct 27): Orange SA raised its profit outlook for the third time this year, driven by growth across all the French mobile carrier’s markets.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation after leases will grow more than 4.5% for the full year, the Paris-based telecommunications company said in a statement on Tuesday. That’s up from a previous forecast of more than 4%.

Third-quarter Ebitdaal rose to €4.14 billion (US$4.6 billion), Orange said, slightly above analysts’ average estimate of €4.09 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

The bulk of Orange’s growth for the period came from its Africa and Middle East markets, both increasingly important engines for the company as competition weighs on its more mature European businesses. It offers mobile, broadband and financial services in the region.

In Europe, the French telecom operator has been seeking greater scale through consolidation. Orange joined rivals Bouygues Telecom and Iliad SA in a €20.4 billion deal to acquire billionaire Patrick Drahi’s SFR in France. If approved by regulators, the transaction would reduce the French market from four major operators to three, potentially easing intense price competition. Orange said it expects the deal to close in the second half of next year, and that negotiations with SFR’s employee works council over the sale process were ongoing.

Earlier this year, Orange also acquired the remaining stake in its MasOrange joint venture in Spain from private equity investors.

See also: Japan vows to address cyber attack on FX with urgency

Like other telecommunications companies in Europe, Orange is trying to evolve beyond its core business, exploring data centres and satellites as potential areas for growth.

Orange partnered with infrastructure manager Morrison in July for a French data-centre venture and is part of a consortium bidding for an EU-subsidised data centre project in France.

It also joined a group effort with Deutsche Telekom AG, Vodafone Group Plc and Telefonica SA to bid for satellite spectrum in Europe to fend off potential competition from SpaceX’s Starlink as the latter expands into mobile connectivity.

title: Meta upsizes equity offering as it seeks almost US$98 bil
article:
(Oct 27): Meta Platforms Inc is seeking to raise as much as US$97.5 billion from selling common and preferred stock, supporting its development in artificial intelligence with one of the largest equity offerings in history.

The company sold US$12.5 billion of preferred shares at US$50 apiece and US$25 billion of common stock at US$625 per share, according to a statement late on Monday. The common stock offering was upsized from US$22.5 billion. Meta also plans to raise as much as about US$60 billion in an at-the-market share sale programme, which allows companies to sell shares in the open market from time to time. The ATM will consist of its planned Class C nonvoting shares.

Nvidia Corp, Advanced Micro Devices Inc and Broadcom Inc agreed to buy as much as US$5 billion of the common shares in aggregate, the company said earlier. Meta intends to use the proceeds to support its investment in AI infrastructure and personal superintelligence.

Meta’s shares slipped 1.7% to US$631.51 at 9.53am in New York. Its shares have fallen 2.7% this year through Friday’s close.

Earlier this year, Alphabet Inc and Intel Corp also held rare stock sales in order to support investment in AI initiatives, which require massive amounts of infrastructure and computing power. Both sales were oversubscribed.

Meta’s CEO Mark Zuckerberg overhauled the company’s AI operation through an aggressive hiring push and has launched new products as well as committed hundreds of billions of dollars to build out the infrastructure needed to support the models. The company also has unveiled a personal AI agent known as Muse and an AI model called Muse Wonder, which leadership says is on par with OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic PBC’s Claude in terms of tasks such as coding.

See also: OCBC draws AI ideas from staff beyond tech teams as it builds skills across the bank

The first part of the offering consisted of 250 million depositary shares that represent a 1/20th interest in mandatory convertible preferred shares. Details of the ATM programme have yet to be determined, the statement shows.

Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs Group Inc are leading Meta’s share offerings, according to the statement.

During its earnings report, Meta announced a new class of nonvoting stock that could ultimately be used to help pay for acquisitions and other expenses. Meta’s Class C shares will be distributed to existing investors through a stock dividend. Holders will get one share of the new stock in what will essentially be a two-for-one stock split, Meta said. It expects trading of the new shares to begin in January.

title: Oil declines as Iran diplomacy picks up before Israeli, US votes
article:
(Oct 27): Oil fell further from a six-month high on hopes diplomacy may avert a flareup in the US-Iran war, with elections looming, including in Israel.

Brent dropped below US$115 a barrel after losing almost 1% in the previous session, while West Texas Intermediate was near US$101. Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey travelled to Tehran for discussions on Monday, with participants agreeing to more talks, IRIB news agency reported.

Elsewhere, Russian President Vladimir Putin is due to meet on Tuesday with his Iranian counterpart, Masoud Pezeshkian, as well as Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, on the sidelines of an energy summit in Moscow. Russia has been a key ally for Tehran during the months-long conflict.

Still, risks remain acute even as crude flows have recovered to around prewar levels, while shipping costs are elevated. In Lebanon, Hezbollah is preparing for a new war after receiving funds from Iran, Reuters said. A Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed four drones targeting the kingdom’s south, and three ballistic missiles aimed at the east, launched by Iran-backed Houthi rebels.

“The market is balancing the bearish signals of a restoration of oil flow from the Middle East and reports of diplomatic Iranian channels remaining open,” said Saul Kavonic, senior energy analyst at MST Marquee. Prices could move substantially either way, depending on whether the conflict escalates, he said.

Global benchmark Brent has surged by almost 90% this year, as the US-Iran war disrupted energy flows and drew Yemen’s Houthi rebels into the conflict, with attacks on Saudi Arabia. Investors are bracing for a packed stretch of potential market catalysts, with Israeli elections on Tuesday, a Federal Reserve (Fed) decision later this week, and the US midterms on Nov 3.

See also: Woodside sells stake in long-stalled Timor-Leste LNG project

In the Israeli contest, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pledging to topple Tehran’s regime, with US President Donald Trump’s backing. His challenger, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, says Iran’s nuclear programme must be stopped, but he’s added that regime change is “not an achievable goal”.

The US midterms offer another potential inflection point, as Trump has suggested that strikes against Iran could resume following the vote. At the weekend, the president told Fox News it was “getting to be decision time” on whether to reach a deal with Tehran or “finish it off”.

For now, Washington’s forces are blockading Iran’s ports to choke off the Islamic Republic’s crude shipments, while assisting flows through the Strait of Hormuz from other Persian Gulf producers. In Monday’s talks, Iran informed Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Pakistan that it’s flexible on a proposal to reopen the waterway in exchange for the lifting of the US curbs in seven days.

See also: European gas hits €97 for first time since 2022 on winter risks
• Brent for December settlement dropped 1% to US$114.63 a barrel at 1.09pm in Singapore.

Despite the fall in futures, Brent’s prompt spread — the difference between its two closest contracts — remains in steep backwardation, a bullish pattern. On Monday, the gap was near US$5 a barrel, up from US$3.69 a week ago.

“Considering the limited odds of the US striking Iran before the midterm elections on Nov 3, versus a much greater chance after the elections, I find it rather odd that the backwardation continues to expand,” said Robert Yawger, director of the energy futures division at Mizuho Securities USA LLC, highlighting the expiry of the December contract at the end of the week.

The Fed will deliver its policy decision on Wednesday, after tightening last month for the first time since 2023 to tackle still-too-hot inflation. In the run-up, Fed officials suggested they were in no hurry to raise interest rates again, despite gains in energy costs such as diesel.

title: Dubai firm’s US$543 mil IPO covered within minutes despite war
article:
(Oct 27): DIP Holding plc drew enough demand to cover its up to US$543 million initial public offering within minutes of opening books, signalling strong appetite for the United Arab Emirates’ first listing since the Iran war began.

Dubai Investments PJSC is offering a 20% stake in DIP at 1.10 dirhams to 1.15 dirhams apiece. At the top of the range, DIP Holding would be valued at 10 billion dirhams. Indicated demand for the offer exceeds the number of shares on offer, according to terms seen by Bloomberg News.

The company is offering investors US$592 million in dividend payouts over the next three years. Based on the expected annual payout of 725 million dirhams for 2027, the price range implies a yield of as much as 7.60%.

Some investors had called for DIP to temper its valuation expectations and offer higher payouts, closer to the roughly 9% yield from developer Emaar Properties PJSC, given geopolitical concerns, Bloomberg News has reported.

The deal comes as the Iran war amplifies a slowdown in Gulf IPO markets. Regional stocks have also come under pressure since the conflict began in late February, with Dubai’s exchange down around 5% this year.

While the IPO market has been slow, deal activity in the Middle East has continued despite the regional conflict. In just the past 24 hours, Apollo Global Management Inc. bought a stake in Mubadala Capital, the alternative asset management arm of Abu Dhabi’s US$385 billion sovereign wealth fund, while Investcorp teamed up with Saudi investors to buy a fire safety and equipment company, one of the first inbound deals in the kingdom since the war with the Iran-backed Houthis escalated.

See also: Anthropic flags ‘existential risks’ in long-awaited IPO filing

DIP Holding owns Dubai Investments Park, a 2,300-hectare (8.9 square mile) development located close to two of Dubai’s major logistics hubs: Jebel Ali Port, which has been severely disrupted by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and Al Maktoum International Airport, which is undergoing a US$35 billion expansion. Among the largest mixed-use projects in the UAE, it houses warehouses, hotels, retailers, schools and healthcare facilities.

Dubai Investments’ wider portfolio includes holdings in roughly 30 businesses across industries including manufacturing, property and financial services. It has previously also earmarked Emirates Glass LLC and district-cooling company Emicool LLC as listing candidates.

The subscription period for the DIP offering will run from Oct 27 to Nov 3, and shares are expected to begin trading on Dubai’s bourse on Nov 11.

title: Jio shares indicated 22% higher in India grey-market trading
article:
(Oct 27): For investors lucky enough to land shares in Jio Platforms Ltd’s US$3.1 billion India-record initial public offering, trading on the unofficial market is fuelling hopes of a big debut pop.

Billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s digital and telecommunications giant has attracted stellar demand across investor categories ahead of its Oct 28 market debut. Investors who got their allocations on Tuesday are now closely watching Jio’s grey-market pricing for clues about how the first day might unfold. The premium over the IPO price has hovered at about 22% for roughly 10 days, unusually resilient for an offering of this size, according to the ipowatch.in and investorgain.com platforms.

Grey market premiums are unregulated and provide no guarantee of where a stock will actually trade once it hits the exchange. Still, they are widely tracked in India as a barometer of demand and listing-day sentiment.

If the pattern holds in the listing, it would make Jio India’s second-most valuable company after parent Reliance Industries Ltd, pushing rival Bharti Airtel Ltd into third place. That prospect is adding to the excitement around an IPO that’s already rewritten records in India’s capital markets. Jio attracted more than US$78 billion in bids and nearly 14 million applications in one of the country’s most anticipated listings.

So far, Jio has been able to defy the usual trend of grey market premiums cooling after an IPO closes, as the initial rush of bidding fades and investors shift their focus to allotments and the eventual listing. After National Stock Exchange of India Ltd's US$2.4 billion IPO, the premium gradually eroded from about 15% to 3% in two weeks and the shares ultimately made a relatively muted debut.

See also: Jio’s record India IPO falls short of record payday for bankers

The optimism is backed by blockbuster subscription numbers. Jio’s IPO was subscribed more than 22 times, with qualified institutional buyers bidding for 71 times the shares reserved for them. Wealthy investors subscribed 14 times their allocation while the retail portion was covered 2.7 times. The offering was fully subscribed within just 100 minutes of opening last week, even as a bruising selloff swept through Indian equities.

title: China’s 5-year government bond yield trades near record low
article:
(Oct 27): China’s five-year government bond yield dropped after the central bank increased its cash injection into the banking system.

The yield on five-year sovereign notes briefly touched 1.34% to head for the lowest closing level on record, based on Chinabond data going back to 2002. It had also briefly declined below the record close on an intraday basis last week.

The People’s Bank of China earlier injected a net RMB1.01 trillion via reverse repurchases in open market operations, the highest daily net injection on record, Bloomberg data show.

title: China property woes bring strains to Huafa’s US$62 bil of debt
article:
(Oct 27): China’s unprecedented property crisis has just reached another flashpoint, as one of the country’s biggest local-government-owned conglomerates struggles with debt payments.

Based in the southern province of Guangdong, Zhuhai Huafa Group Co missed payments on two trust products that were due recently, people familiar with the matter said on Monday. The firm, which has helped build landmarks such as the 330m tall Zhuhai Tower skyscraper, has also been asking to extend loans from at least three banks.

That makes it the largest company heavily reliant on the property sector to try pushing back debt payments since China Vanke Co, once the country’s biggest developer, took similar steps about a year ago.

The development underscores how China’s years-long real estate debt woes are still spreading despite recent signs of stabilisation in the housing market. Huafa has developed over 200 residential projects across China. The conglomerate had RMB413 billion of interest-bearing liabilities, including bank and trust loans as well as bonds, as of March, according to a company document this month.

“Huafa is facing the same challenges as other Chinese developers but it also plays such a crucial role in the local economy that local governments are highly likely to step in and support it,” said Yao Yu, CEO and founder of credit research firm RatingDog. “The eventual repayment outlook of Huafa’s bonds is not overly pessimistic.”

See also: Seven adjoining Hillview Terrace factories launched for sale at $51.6 mil

Still, the news this week sparked sharp declines in bonds and shares tied to the group, which had just priced a RMB1 billion note in the domestic market at the relatively low cost of 2.07% only a few days ago.

One of Huafa’s offshore yuan-denominated bonds was last indicated down by a record 17% Tuesday, bringing it to about 74% of face value.

Shares of Zhuhai Huafa Properties Co, the real estate arm of Huafa Group, fell as much as 8.9% in Shanghai Tuesday, to the lowest intra-day level in more than a month.

See also: One Comcentre earns ‘industry-leading’ customer experience rating

Unlike Vanke, which is only partially backed by a state-owned firm in Shenzhen, Huafa is wholly owned by the Guangdong government, with Zhuhai’s State-Owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission holding about 93.5% and the provincial finance department owning the remainder.

Local rating firm China Lianhe Credit Rating affirmed Huafa’s AAA rating earlier this year, despite its heavy debt burden, weakening profitability and its high reliance on external financing. The credit assessor cited expectations of strong local government support, given Huafa’s status as a major conglomerate owned by Zhuhai.

After a downward spiral for five years, China’s home prices fell at a slower pace last month, fuelling hopes that the property market is turning a corner. China’s government recently turned to mortgage subsidies and changes to bank lending policies to step up efforts to support the economy.

Huafa, which derived about half of its revenue from property development and urban operations last year while also running businesses spanning financial services and technology, had blamed the property downturn as the main reason for its profitability swings.

It reported a total loss of RMB16.9 billion last year and had about RMB765 billion in total assets as of March.

“Local government-backed Chinese developers are likely to remain under pressure amid weak homebuyer sentiment, falling property sales and limited fiscal capacity at many regional governments,” said Andrew Chan, credit analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence. “Unlike centrally backed SOEs, they face weaker funding access and refinancing support.”

title: Chinese firm’s investor dispute shows dark side of HK listings
article:
(Oct 27): A dispute involving a Chinese technology firm at the centre of a deal-rigging probe is pulling back the curtain on the sometimes murky details of dealmaking around Hong Kong initial public offerings, just as regulators mount a historic crackdown on suspected market distortions.

The fallout at Tianju Dihe Suzhou Technology Co underscores concerns raised by the city’s securities watchdog. The company is under scrutiny for suspected IPO rigging, its shares have been suspended and senior executives have resigned after a deal linked to a cornerstone backer soured. Both the company and the investor are in the crosshairs of an investigation looking into suspected schemes to create false demand. One of the key red flags the regulator has advised market participants to be vigilant about is listing companies making substantial investments or loans to prospective investors.

At the centre of the episode is a series of transactions around Tianju Dihe’s 2024 IPO. A forensic probe, commissioned by the company after audit questions emerged, found that the data processor invested with two firms after limited vetting. When the notes allegedly matured at dates Tianju Dihe thought had been agreed on, the money never returned. It’s unclear whether the regulatory action was triggered by the probe or started independently of it.

The Suzhou-based company invested in US$6 million worth of so-called cash-management notes with Reynold Lemkins Group Asia Ltd — a cornerstone investor in its IPO — and another US$4 million with Kaufmann & Company Pan-Asia Ltd, a company Tianju Dihe later said had been in a business relationship with Reynold Lemkins. Tianju Dihe is now pursuing legal action in a dispute over the notes, alleging that Reynold Lemkins and Kaufmann didn’t make repayments or distributions.

Tianju Dihe and Yang Dong, a person tied to Kaufmann, didn’t respond to requests for comment. A query sent to an email address listed on Reynold Lemkins’ website couldn’t be delivered.

Hong Kong regulators recently highlighted concerns about the overreliance on IPO-related networks and intermediaries as they stepped up the scrutiny of the city’s booming market for listings. Tianju Dihe’s disclosure offers a rare glimpse into the inner workings of relationships forged during a deal process and how they can evolve into subsequent investment transactions.

See also: Chinese PCB maker Dongshan raises US$1.3 bil in HK listing

The Securities and Futures Commission this month announced one of the most sweeping enforcement actions in Hong Kong’s history. The regulator suspended bubble tea maker Sichuan Baicha Baidao Industrial Co’s stock as it investigates a suspected case of IPO rigging, while it also issued restriction notices to 31 brokers, prohibiting them from dealing with or processing assets relating to two syndicates on three listings.

Separately, the SFC said it had identified cases in which listing applicants may have entered into undisclosed arrangements with investors, without specifying the deals. It pinpointed payments made by listing candidates — loans or investments in favour of investors — among red flags that can help market participants identify “dubious arrangements”.

As part of the measures, the watchdog also restricted 29 brokers from dealing with assets of up to HK$285 million in client accounts related to Tianju Dihe’s IPO.

See also: Hong Kong IPO red flags include sudden loans and secret handshakes

The company detailed its findings before the SFC this month said it was taking action against Tianju Dihe, Reynold Lemkins, Kaufmann and Liu Haoran, an individual, for suspected fraud to create the false or artificial appearance of IPO demand.

Tianju Dihe, whose stock has been suspended since April 2025, made the disclosures after the stock exchange ordered an independent investigation into audit issues. The probe found the company had not verified Reynold Lemkins and Kaufmann’s licences or qualifications, and that the firm had relied on due-diligence work conducted by professional parties rather than conducting its own vetting.

The company was introduced to Reynold Lemkins for a potential cornerstone investment by its then-sole sponsor of the deal, it said, citing the investigator’s finding. Listing documents now show Citic Securities Co as the IPO’s sole sponsor.

Tianju Dihe had said its subscription of Reynold Lemkins notes wasn’t an indirect benefit or side arrangement given for being a cornerstone investor.

As a form of remedy, the company’s founder Zuo Lei agreed to take up all US$10 million of the notes. Zuo, who was chairman and chief executive officer, and two executives resigned in August as a result of the need for “improvement in the company’s internal control system and a need to implement additional internal control procedures", the company said in a filing.

Reynold Lemkins describes itself as an investment firm. Among the Hong Kong IPO investments the firm has made are supply chain firm EDA Group Holdings Ltd and insurance-agency service provider Zhongmiao Holdings Qingdao Co, according to listing documents. Reynold Lemkins was a cornerstone investor in seven Hong Kong IPOs since 2024, according to listing documents and data compiled by Dealogic.

Liu, who goes by the Western name Kris, has served as the company’s chairman of the China region and chief investment officer, according to a biography on the Greenwich Economic Forum’s website. The biography says Liu has been involved in more than US$25 billion in investments and transactions including IPOs.

title: Yangzijiang Maritime to sell six vessels for US$308 million
article:
Yangzijiang Maritime Development is selling six newbuild vessels for a total consideration of US$308 ($394) million. The vessels comprise: two 49,500 deadweight tonnage (DWT) medium-range tankers scheduled to be delivered in 2027 and 2028; and four 49,800 DWT newbuild medium-range tankers for delivery in 2027 and 2028.

So far for 2026, the company has signed sales contracts for a total of 18 newbuild vessels with an aggregate gross value of US$805 million. The company’s newbuild portfolio, including options currently stands at 98.

“One of Yangzijiang Maritime’s unique value propositions lies in our ability to consistently originate attractive maritime investment opportunities, organize and build value through strategic asset ownership at favourable prices, and realise returns at opportune points in the maritime cycle,” says executive chairman Ren Yuanlin.

“Our proactive asset monetisation strategy creates a virtuous cycle of value realisation via asset sales and capital reinvestment into new vessel orders, enabling us to pursue further growth opportunities and create greater long-term value for shareholders.”

As at 12 pm on Oct 27, shares in the company are down one cent, or 1.7%, to 56.5 cents.

title: Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo draws early complaints of the screen cracking
article:
(Oct 27): The iPhone Duo, one of Apple Inc’s biggest new products in years, is drawing a growing number of complaints from customers who say the foldable display cracked after just hours or days of use.

In these cases, customers reported hearing a crunching sound when unfolding the phone, followed by a large crack forming along the centre crease. Some users also experienced a white patch or other display malfunction on the right side of the screen.

Reports of the problem first surfaced on Reddit and other social media sites. Bloomberg News has since independently verified the issue with more than half a dozen customers, who provided photos showing damage to their devices or evidence of their support conversations with Apple.

Apple acknowledged the issue in a statement, saying it was “aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units”.

“If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement,” the Cupertino, California-based company said. Most Duos aren’t affected by the problem, and the units that are impacted exhibit the defect quickly, Apple said.

“I went to unfold it and it felt stuck/harder/slower to open than usual. And when I opened it it had the lines on the screen,” Tom Battle, an Apple customer from San Diego, told Bloomberg. “You could feel a bump or loose piece under the display.”

See also: Alibaba wins challenge to Pentagon’s Chinese army blacklisting

Venture capitalist Jonathan King had a similar experience, saying he heard a crunch-like sound when opening his device on Monday.

“I had all intent to post a positive review of my Duo experience today, until it happened to me,” King said. “The smaller outer screen works just fine, but the inner screen is now unusable,” he said, adding that the device thinks he is touching the inner screen when he is not.

While the problem appears to affect only a subset of units, it represents an embarrassing setback for Apple, which spent more than a decade developing the device and touted its superior durability, hinge design and display technology.

See also: Microsoft to offer buyouts to 60,000 workers in new cost cut

The Duo, which went on sale on Friday, represents the company’s first foray into foldable phones — and the biggest-ever design change to the iPhone, Apple’s largest source of revenue. Like other foldable phones, the device has a smaller screen on its outer surface and can be opened to reveal a larger display.

Chief executive officer John Ternus previously dismissed competing Android foldables as “cheap and crappy”, while the company’s head of hardware engineering, Tom Marieb, encouraged customers to hold Apple “accountable” for the screen crease’s durability. During the phone’s development, Apple worked to reduce the visibility of the crease in the middle of the opened display — a problem that has plagued previous foldables.

Bloomberg didn’t encounter the issue on one review unit provided by Apple or another device purchased independently.

“I was reading Apple News and decided to open the display to enjoy it, and that’s when I saw the crack line and bruising,” a user who goes by Centrino31A told Bloomberg. “There is no damage to the outside of the phone nor to the inner display surface. It is pristine. The issue is the underlying display.”

The customer said his local Apple retail store in Richmond, Virginia, called the issue a defect that required a replacement, but the location had no Genius Bar customer-support appointments available. Apple then sent him to another store, which conducted testing to confirm there was no accidental damage. But that location had no inventory, so he is still waiting for a replacement device.

Centrino31A said he understands that first-generation devices can have unexpected issues, but that it was “extremely frustrating” that stores didn’t have separate inventory for addressing manufacturing problems, particularly for a device that starts at US$1,999 ($2,560).

In all cases, users said they felt a bump under the display near where the crack started. Repair platform iFixit, which disassembles products to study their components, said it believes the issue is caused by a piece of the hinge failing and cracking the screen, rather than a problem with the display panel itself.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

The company has faced issues with new iPhone hardware in the past, including the iPhone 6 Plus in 2014, which would bend easily, and the iPhone 4 in 2010, which sometimes lost reception when users touched the antenna cutout around the device. In both cases, the company emerged from the problems relatively unscathed.

The latest difficulties show that “even a company with Apple’s engineering resources and supply chain discipline faces a steep learning curve in foldables”, according to IDC analyst Francisco Jeronimo.

Samsung Electronics Co, which pioneered the foldable field, also had problems with its first Galaxy Fold in 2019, Jeronimo noted. “It also showed that a fast and transparent response can contain the damage to a category,” he said, adding that Apple’s move on Monday to send users to customer care is “the right first step”.

Vishnu Rajkumar, an Apple customer who said he has used previous foldable phones from OnePlus and Samsung, also experienced the Duo issue. “I was setting up my apps and wanted to check how Outlook works in the wider inner screen,” he said. “I tried opening the screen and found an unusual tightness.”

After applying a bit more pressure, “the screen started bleeding”, he said. “Initially the line was small, and it increased further after multiple folds.” Rajkumar, who lives in Chennai, India, was able to locate a replacement device at an authorised reseller and said that model hasn’t had any issues during his first 24 hours of use.

Another user, Surya Mangi of Allen, Texas, said the inner screen cracked after about 30 hours of ownership during normal opening of the display. “Trying to replace but no Apple Store around so asking me to send in and be phoneless for over a week,” he said. Apple is ultimately shipping Mangi a replacement by express mail.

Apple employees said the company hasn’t provided any official guidance to its retail stores or customer service agents about the problem as of the initial publication of this story. But a team is investigating the issue. In some cases, Apple engineers are trying to obtain affected devices for analysis.

One customer, Justin Lokos, said Apple did what is known as an Early Field Failure Analysis on his device. “I gave as much detail as possible,” he said in a note. “All of the employees in store were very intrigued (imagine I was the first person there to have this issue).” He received a replacement at Apple’s Fifth Avenue store in New York.

Lokos said he was sitting on his living room couch at 5.40pm using the iPhone Duo to order Grubhub, but the experience wasn’t ideal on the outer screen because the app isn’t yet optimised for the new design. He thought it would work better unfolded, but when he opened the device, he heard a crunching sound and the display cracked.

Another user, Jainam Shah, said his iPhone Duo’s hinge felt perfectly normal until one particular unfolding, when it suddenly became noticeably stiffer. “I continued opening it, heard an audible crack and immediately noticed the bright vertical and horizontal lines across the inner display.”

Shah said there had been no drops, impacts or unusual pressure on the phone. “Took it straight back to the Apple Store, where the employees were just as surprised,” he said. “They replaced it immediately and asked if I’d be comfortable having engineering reach out to understand what happened.”

title: Iron ore declines to two-year low as demand outlook weakens
article:
(Oct 27): Iron ore dropped to the lowest level in more than two years on a weaker demand outlook and rising supply through year-end.

Benchmark futures in Singapore fell as much as 1.4% to US$89.25 a tonne, the lowest intraday level since September 2024. Prices on the Dalian Commodity Exchange were also at a two-year low. China is approaching a seasonally weak period for steel consumption while elevated oil prices have raised concerns about the global economic outlook, leaving few catalysts for a potential rebound.

“Iron ore is likely to stay soft through November,” said Mengtian Jiang, chief ferrous analyst at Horizon Insights. Prices could extend declines toward US$86 to US$85 a tonne, with the last two months of the year historically the weakest period for steel consumption, she added.

“Against elevated port stocks, mills are restocking only hand-to-mouth and have grown desensitised to macro stimulus,” Jiang said. Iron ore shipments from the four major miners, including Rio Tinto Group and BHP Group, are expected to rise by as much as 18 million tonnes in the fourth quarter, while Guinea’s Simandou mine continues to ramp up output, she said.

A stand-off between state-backed buyer China Mineral Resources Group and key miners had injected a supply-risk premium into the market, but that has eased following resolutions, including with Rio Tinto. Still, Australia’s Fortescue Ltd remains stuck in talks with CMRG over a potential deal.

See also: Soybeans hit two-month low as Lula’s win lifts China trade outlook

Iron ore was 1.2% lower at US$89.40 a tonne as of 10.45am Singapore time. On the London Metal Exchange, copper rose 0.2% to US$14,360 a tonne as risk sentiment got a boost from a fresh rally in artificial intelligence stocks. Aluminium fell, and zinc held near its highest close this month.

title: Woodside sells stake in long-stalled Timor-Leste LNG project
article:
(Oct 27): Woodside Energy Group Ltd has sold its operating interest in the long-stalled Greater Sunrise liquefied natural gas (LNG) project to a Timor-Leste state-owned company.

The sale of the 33.44% stake is worth as much as US$200 million, Woodside said Tuesday in a statement, although most of that is dependent on the project being built. The small nation has long pushed for the development of the two fields that make up Greater Sunrise and a LNG plant in a bid to tap potentially billions of dollars of revenue.

Timor Gap will now control the entire project, after last month agreeing to buy out a third shareholder, Osaka Gas Corp. An independent assessment from 2018 estimated the development cost at US$15.6 billion.

For years Woodside and the Timorese government have argued over whether to build the liquefaction plant locally or pipe the gas to Australia. The fields have contingent resources of 5.1 trillion cubic feet of gas and 226 million barrels of condensate, according to Timor Gap.
